_comment: Gate 0 APP-SERVER launch-surface amendment (reports/2026-07-24-gate0-prereg-amendment-appserver.md) -- the app-server-transport sibling of the FROZEN eval/fixtures/gate0_expected_pins_red.json (that file is unedited; this is a NEW, separately named fixture, never overwriting it). Consumed the SAME way: tools/check_gate0_codex.py::audit()'s expected_pins argument (schema_version 2, all PIN_FIELDS present), for a run launched by tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py instead of tools/run_gate0_codex.ps1.
_what_changed_vs_the_frozen_exec_based_p: ONLY the launch SURFACE (exec -> app-server transport, tools/run_gate0_codex.ps1 -> tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py) and the approval MECHANISM (codex exec's stdin-EOF auto-decline -> codex app-server's answerable RPC, answered `accept` by tools/gate0_appserver_client.py). Neither is a PIN_FIELD in this file's own vocabulary -- the launcher's own identity is tracked separately, in eval/fixtures/gate0_signature.appserver.json's `expected_launcher_sha256` (a NEW field on that OTHER fixture, not on this one). Every field below is UNCHANGED from the frozen exec-based pin -- VERIFIED during this build (not assumed): (a) codex_path/codex_executable_sha256/codex_version are unaffected by which SUBCOMMAND (`exec` vs `app-server`) is invoked -- same binary; (b) brain_config_sha256 was independently recomputed by tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::render_brain_config_toml() for model=gpt-5.6-sol + the SAME developer_instructions string and hash-compared byte-for-byte against this exact value (ab7e54c1...) -- MATCH; (c) task_sha256 was likewise recomputed by tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::task_text_for('red') and hash-compared against this exact value (306751c3...) -- MATCH; (d) world_image_tag/world_image_id/host_code_sha256/image_code_sha256/mcp_servers_observed/mcp_tools_observed/critical_config_transport/auth_method/paid_execution_enabled/readiness are all structural/image constants, unaffected by transport.
_paid_execution_enabled_note: Stays `false` -- this field's OWN documented contract (see the frozen pin's _source_paid_execution_enabled) is 'the launcher contains no `codex exec` path', i.e. structural, not 'did this run spend money'. tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py invokes `codex app-server`, never `codex exec` -- the field's literal meaning still holds for this transport.
_config_sha256_and_codex_mcp_list_sha256: Left as the SAME launch-invocation-dependent placeholder as the frozen pin (never a real value here either) -- these two fields depend on the launch OutputDir's absolute paths and the frozen world image ID (now baked into the mount args), so they cannot be a single fixed value even with a fixed commit. RESOLVED AT LAUNCH TIME (not left dangling): tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::resolve_expected_pins() substitutes both fields with THIS run's own pre-turn-computed handshake-receipt.json values (config.toml/codex-mcp-list.json are rendered and hashed entirely BEFORE the paid codex app-server turn spawns -- see _run_real -- so the substituted value is a function of the launch spec alone, never of anything the paid model said or did) before calling tools/check_gate0_codex.py::audit(), refusing (ValueError) if this marker is ever missing here first. Mirrors the exec path's own documented recompute recipe (this file's exec sibling eval/fixtures/gate0_expected_pins_red.json:_source_config_sha256) and eval/fixtures/gate0_signature.example.json's own 'expected_config_sha256: this launch's freshly computed handshake-receipt.json:config_sha256' contract -- check_gate0_codex.py itself is never edited or given a CONSTRAINT-skip rule (confirmed the exec path never had one either: reports/2026-07-21-gate0-readiness-final-v2.md Sec.3 shows the exec path hitting this identical pin_mismatch on a real receipt against the raw static fixture, masked only by NO_LEAK from a missing transcript, never actually fixed there). tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::verify_launch_signature_unchanged() re-hashes the on-disk config.toml/codex-mcp-list.json immediately after the turn and fails loud before this substitution if they drifted from what the receipt recorded pre-turn -- a narrower, fail-fast duplicate of check_gate0_codex.py's own frozen _artifact_failures re-hash-and-compare, not a replacement for it.
_tool_schema_sha256_note:
RE-DERIVED 2026-07-24 for the app-server surface's OWN serialization (was previously e55bb819... INHERITED verbatim from the exec-based pin's PowerShell `ConvertTo-Json -Compress` serialization -- a byte-format mismatch against tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::_run_real's actual `json.dumps(tools) + "
"` write to mcp-tools.json, producing a guaranteed pin_mismatch on every real run despite an identical, correct tool inventory). Computed via a $0 seam-check (`python -m tools.gate0_appserver_arm --arm red --out-dir <dir> --seam-check --with-tools-list`, i.e. tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::docker_tools_list()'s live tools/list JSON-RPC handshake -- no codex/model call) against this file's own pinned world_image_id (sha256:5bfabc75...), serialized with `json.dumps(tools) + "
"` (the exact bytes _run_real writes to mcp-tools.json), SHA-256 of those bytes. Observed inventory matched the frozen red allowlist exactly. Read-only corroboration (not the source): byte-identical to the real, already-completed Arm R run's own handshake-receipt.json:tool_schema_sha256 at runs/gate0_paid/red/ -- expected, since the schema is a pure function of world_mcp.py (parity-verified) and the app-server's serialization is deterministic; the seam-check was run independently of that receipt, not copied from it. **2026-07-25 CORRECTION (adversarial review of PR #163, correction 1):** as of 2026-07-24 this claim was NOT actually reproducible from `--seam-check --with-tools-list` -- that flag only reported tool NAMES inline and never wrote an artifact or computed a hash (confirmed: the one committed seam-check artifact, `runs/gate0_seam_check/red/seam_check.json`, has no tools-list section and no miniwob sibling). `tools/gate0_appserver_arm.py::_run_seam_check` now actually writes `mcp-tools.json` (`json.dumps(tools) + "
"`, byte-identical to `_run_real`'s write) and records `tool_schema_sha256` in `seam_check.json` when `--with-tools-list` is passed. Re-run live against this file's pinned image 2026-07-25 (real docker, $0, no codex/model call): observed `tool_schema_sha256` = `102e4cb37c4b5412c149c706c5862f412934bee7d10c105478afa2db5c877c3e` -- MATCHES the value pinned below exactly. The recipe this note describes is now genuinely reproducible, not merely asserted.
